summary: Fougeil Veterinary Diagnostics, Inc. (client) makes companion-animal point-of-care chemistry and hematology analyzers and their reagent consumables. In 2023 it appointed Treireis Animal Health Distribution, LLC as its exclusive U.S. distributor under a Delaware-law Distribution Agreement. Treireis's parent, Treireis Holdings, Inc., guarantees Treireis's payment obligations. The folder holds the Distribution Agreement, Order Form, First Amendment, launch side letter, Service Level Schedule, Parent Guaranty, Quality Agreement, Fougeil's October 2026 notice letter, a superseded prior draft and the current price list. Six issues are planted. (1) Five-year automatic renewals result from the renewal clause read with the Order Form term. (2) A worldwide, all-channel, post-term non-compete binds Fougeil far beyond the U.S. companion-animal field. (3) Distributor's assignment is unrestricted. (4) The First Amendment's renumbering of the indemnities flips the uncapped carve-out onto Fougeil's own indemnity. (5) The guaranty selects New York law and courts. (6) Fougeil's notice converting exclusivity for the Contract Year 3 purchase shortfall was sent after the 60-day exercise window closed.

issues.label: automatic renewal
issues.description: D1 Section 3.2 provides that the Agreement automatically renews for successive Renewal Terms 'each equal in length to the Initial Term' unless a party gives non-renewal notice at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term. Read alone, the clause looks routine. D2 Section 2 sets the Initial Term at sixty (60) months, which also looks routine. Read together, every renewal is a further five-year term. Fougeil stays locked into an exclusive appointment, and into the D1 Section 2.3 non-compete, for five more years each time a single 90-day deadline is missed. D1 has no termination-for-convenience right to escape that lock-in.
detect_terms: equal in length to the Initial Term
issues.expected_finding: Read with the Order Form's 60-month Initial Term, Section 3.2 renews the exclusive appointment automatically for further five-year terms unless notice is given at least 90 days before expiry. Fougeil should calendar the deadline and renegotiate to shorter (e.g., one-year) renewal terms or a termination-for-convenience right.

issues.label: overbroad exclusivity
issues.description: The commercial deal recorded in D2 Section 3 is exclusivity in the United States for companion-animal point-of-care chemistry and hematology analyzers and consumables. D1 Section 2.3, however, bars Fougeil and its Affiliates from selling or distributing any 'Competing Product' anywhere in the world, through any channel, during the Term and for 24 months afterward. 'Competing Product' covers any veterinary diagnostic analyzer, test or reagent, including livestock, equine and reference-laboratory products. Under D1 Section 17.3 the Distribution Agreement prevails over the Order Form, so the narrower Order Form scope does not limit Section 2.3. The clause blocks Fougeil's non-U.S. sales and its other product lines, and it risks unenforceability or antitrust scrutiny as broader than any legitimate interest.
issues.expected_finding: Section 2.3 imposes a worldwide, all-channel, all-veterinary-diagnostics non-compete lasting 24 months after the Term. Because the Agreement prevails over the Order Form, this overrides the agreed U.S. companion-animal point-of-care scope. It should be narrowed to the Order Form's Territory and Field, and the post-term tail should be deleted.

issues.label: unrestricted assignment
issues.description: D1 Section 15.1 provides only that 'Supplier shall not assign' the Agreement without Distributor's prior written consent. Nothing restricts Distributor. Section 15.4 states that the Agreement binds and benefits the parties' 'successors and assigns'. Under Delaware law, contract rights are freely assignable absent a clear restriction. Read together, the two sections let Treireis assign its exclusive U.S. appointment, along with the benefit of Fougeil's non-compete, without consent and to anyone, including a competing diagnostics manufacturer or its distribution arm. Fougeil would have no consent right and no termination right.
issues.expected_finding: Because Section 15.1 restrains only Supplier and Section 15.4 extends the Agreement to assigns, Treireis can freely assign its exclusive distributorship, including to a Fougeil competitor. The clause should be made mutual, require consent, treat a change of control as an assignment, and give Fougeil a termination right on any assignment to a competitor.

issues.label: liability cap carve-out conflict
issues.description: D1 Section 12.3(a) excludes from the Section 12.2 liability cap 'a party's obligations under Section 11.1'. In D1 as signed, Section 11.1 is Distributor's indemnity of Supplier (handling, cold-chain storage, unauthorized product claims and Distributor regulatory violations), and Section 11.2 is Supplier's indemnity. That arrangement favours Fougeil. D3 Section 2 deletes Section 11 in its entirety and replaces it with a reordered Section 11 in which new Section 11.1 is 'Supplier Indemnification' and new Section 11.2 is Distributor's indemnity. D3 makes no conforming change to Section 12.3. Under D1 Section 17.3 signed amendments take precedence. The combined effect is that Fougeil's own indemnity becomes uncapped, while Treireis's indemnity of Fougeil becomes subject to the 12-month fees cap.
issues.expected_finding: Because the First Amendment renumbers the indemnities without conforming Section 12.3(a), the cap carve-out now leaves Fougeil's Supplier indemnity uncapped and caps Treireis's indemnity of Fougeil at 12 months' fees. A corrective amendment should point the carve-out expressly to the Distributor indemnity, now Section 11.2.
detect_terms2: deleted in its entirety and replaced

issues.label: governing law mismatch
issues.description: D1 Sections 16.1 and 16.2 select Delaware law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the state or federal courts in Wilmington, Delaware. D6 Section 9, the Parent Guaranty by which Treireis Holdings, Inc. guarantees Treireis's payment obligations under D1, selects New York law and the exclusive jurisdiction of courts in New York County. The guaranty is not among the documents ranked in D1's order of precedence, so nothing reconciles the two clauses. Fougeil could not join the guarantor in a Delaware action against Treireis. It would face parallel proceedings, possibly inconsistent rulings on the underlying obligation, and guarantor defenses under a different body of law.
detect_terms: laws of the State of New York
issues.expected_finding: The Parent Guaranty's New York law and exclusive New York forum conflict with the Distribution Agreement's Delaware law and Wilmington forum. Fougeil would have to sue the guarantor separately, with risk of inconsistent results. The guaranty should be amended to Delaware law and the same forum, or at least a non-exclusive forum allowing joinder.

issues.label: expired notice window
issues.description: D1 Section 4.4 lets Supplier convert Distributor's appointment to non-exclusive for a minimum-purchase shortfall by written notice 'within sixty (60) days after the end of' the applicable Contract Year. D1 Section 1 defines a Contract Year as each 12-month period beginning July 1, so Contract Year 3 ended June 30, 2026 and the window closed August 29, 2026. D7, Fougeil's letter dated October 28, 2026, invokes the Contract Year 3 shortfall to convert the appointment to non-exclusive. That letter, and nothing later in the folder showing acceptance, records Fougeil's position that the conversion is effective. The letter falls about two months outside the window, so Treireis can treat it as ineffective and its exclusivity continues.
issues.expected_finding: The October 28, 2026 notice was sent after the conversion right for the Contract Year 3 shortfall lapsed on August 29, 2026 (60 days after the June 30, 2026 Contract Year end), so it is likely ineffective and Treireis remains exclusive. Fougeil should not rely on the conversion and should instead seek a negotiated amendment or preserve the right for the Contract Year 4 shortfall window.
